key_idea: Grade the space by degree after orthogonalizing with respect to the weight |p|, so that multiplication by h = parity·sgn(p) vanishes between grades whose indices sum to less than n−d. The block energies then form a coupling of two Bin(n,1/2) laws with a one-sided constraint, and an anticommutator Hilbert–Schmidt bound recovers the sensitive edges.
reason: The proof recasts sensitivity as equal-sign edges after multiplying by parity. A weighted orthogonal-polynomial grading turns the degree condition into a support constraint on a coupling of binomials, and the short one-sided coupling lemma finishes the argument; this is surprising and conceptually unified. The edge-recovery lemma still needs some careful energy bookkeeping (operator-norm bounds via the J and W conjugations, the deficit accounting), so it falls short of a pure book proof.
